title: FEEDBACK, anyone have used LLM for lore base
author: Nervous_Teach_5596
selftext:
So basically that, I want to do a game, I have made a half world, races (~7), major cities(~5), places (~13), technology, rituals, even politics (~4 bands) and religions (2 major ones, ~5 in total), all done by the model (because I wanted to explore this, and get my imagination floating in a container, not on freely and don't get nothing connected at the end), yet some there's some logical corners to polish/connect (and some roads that don't exist at all on the lore)

I think I can get a game out there, I want to do (I think I can do) the history by myself, but not sure if using it as base is a good idea and that's what I wanted feedback if someone has done that, I don't want to do a 5 development years with AI game, but maybe 1~2 years (of weekends), I'm just want to do a simple MVP RPG

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
I used AI to write the story for a RPG game and I was told the story is predictable and cliche. 

I think it is okay if you just need AI to finish up the lore so you can work on other parts of your game

just don't expect the lore to impress anyone and hopefully the lore isn't the selling point of your RPG

replies.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
replies.body:
Well that is on part why I want to do the history by myself, because the LLM itself takes the initiative to say, this is too cliche, I had tried to do also 4 starts because I was exploring the idea mostly, and the LLM have done, one cliche, one even more cliche ( and literally it said, this is the cliche start ) , a mistery one, a horror history, yet that is somehow normal as the actual industry has tried almost each approach

The idea mostly isn't to shine like a star, is do some I want to do, play, and also maybe getting ideas for the next one, also share the link if you, can, and want, so I can try also (the cliche isn't bad, if well done)

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
the "well done" part is very much the issue here

I think if you are a writer, you may be able to fix it up

I am not, so... I have the same issue with art: stuff look okay to me but everyone else think its bad

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: I think it all depends how you're going to use the lore. My game started out with hand written lore and then I used those as an example for an LLM to helpful flesh out the world.

replies.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
replies.body: I want it as a constraint for ideas, so the ideas don't get far, I have tried to do this by myself, but I got carried over, and over, and never *finished* (this is what I want mostly, than the next star indie game)

comments.author: Varrianda
comments.body: You need to cut your scope way back if you want to finish this. AI is good but it’s not magic

replies.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
replies.body: That's the why I have tried this way, so I keep it contained on that I have done and center on the corners/game history

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body: What specifically are you trying to do? As in: write the plot, write world history, other world building, use it ingame at runtime...?

replies.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
replies.body: Just the world base history, like some base to get over, and do a game history over that

comments.author: Mobile_Bonus4983
comments.body: While doing ttrpg this depends on the model. A lot of them Chatgpt, Gemini and Claude are taking away roleplay from the model. Glm5.1 is one of them that still has it inside. So imagination is being stripped away. Iterating a story instead of one shot is important.

replies.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
replies.body: Well that's the only that yet Grok has yet, (It took me 7 days because limits (free tier), iterations, output limits, and somehow at the middle of the way they've cut the ASCCI art module, yet no the vision model somehow (image ->analysis->text)), Kimi and DeepSeek are really bad at this, I mean, you try to make anything, and they just cut on round corners, but are really good visualizing maps (and making images with matploth, even the second one that don't see at all)

comments.author: Noble_Nexus
comments.body:
I think LLM are better for brainstorming than actually write. The lore for a world is a very personal thing and it carries that author feeling and way of think.

Try throw some ideas, write yourself and then take it to the LLM for consistency and hunt for holes. This way you can use the power of the tool and still retain the creativity sovereign over your lore.

replies.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
replies.body: That is actually the idea, get a "world", polish, and make myself the history of the game then, (I'm not a profesional writer but the actual idea of the world is some that make me do at least to write some)

replies.author: Noble_Nexus
replies.body:
The difference between a professional writer and an amateur is experience. Try your hand on it if you feel like it. Also the more you participate in the process the better. Use the tool as a helping hand and sometimes a guide, but avoid let it doing most of it for a more authentic result.

Good luck with the project!

comments.author: kkogong07
comments.body:
Sounds like you've already got the right mindset — using it as a constraint rather than a crutch. One thing I'd add: regardless of whether the lore came from an LLM, a writing partner, or a random generator, the final call is always yours. You're the one deciding what stays, what gets cut, and what actually fits the game you want to make. That doesn't change just because the source was AI.  
  
The way you're describing it — polish the corners yourself, write the actual story on top of it — that's pretty much how any collaborative worldbuilding works. The output is only as good as the judgment you bring to it. If the world feels inspirational to you, that's what matters. Own it.
